card: See each path before Linux cleanup touches it.
title: linux-cleanup and named paths
intro: linux-cleanup begins by naming the paths it could touch. The dry-run gives you a chance to read the list first.

sections.heading: What is linux-cleanup for?
sections.body: It clears Linux disk and cache space with a developer-aware catalogue.

sections.heading: What does it show before a change?
sections.body: Before anything changes, it tells you which paths it would touch.

sections.heading: How is deletion controlled?
sections.body: A real dry-run and one deletion chokepoint keep the actual removal in a single place.

sections.heading: Where does linux-cleanup fit beside LifeWell?
sections.body: LifeWell keeps personal entries that can be read back. linux-cleanup deals with a different kind of keeping — deciding which disk paths may go.
